annotations.text:
Round 3 — your picks applied:

• Flat header, count row removed
• View toggle moved INTO the header row, left of the K menu (my recommendation — nothing is stranded and a whole row disappears)
• Buckets: C cards
• Command bar: Bar 3, mode chip now icon-only as its own little card beside the bar

Two alternate homes for the toggle sit to the right, if the header-row placement feels too busy. Serif header moved to Round 1.

Synthesis

Header is now a single row: date left, view toggle + K menu right, week strip under it, straight on the paper. The bottom row is the detached mode card + command bar.

Watch: the toggle and the K circle sit close — if it feels crowded in use, the cycle-button alternate slims that corner.

Toggle alternate — cycle button

One icon button showing the current view; tap cycles Buckets → List → Schedule, long-press opens the full picker. Slimmest header-row option.
Tradeoff: current state is only legible if you know the icons, and cycling is awkward with more than three views.

Toggle alternate — in the mode sheet

The view segmented control moves into the sheet the mode card opens, under the surface list — 'where am I / how do I see it' become one control and the header carries nothing but date + K.
Tradeoff: switching views becomes two taps, which matters if you flip Buckets/Schedule many times a day.

1 — Cards (from C) — PICKED for now

One white card per bucket on the paper backdrop. Strongest bucket identity and drag targets.
Tradeoff: three borders + three shadows of visual weight, and empty buckets still cost a whole card.

2 — Single sheet (C expanded toward B)

One continuous card holds every bucket as a section, full-width hairlines between sections. Calmest option, most rows per screen.
Tradeoff: weakest bucket boundaries — drop targets and 'which bucket am I in' rely on the section headers alone.

3 — Sheet + spines

The single sheet, but each section carries its time-of-day spine (ported from the desktop bucket cards) instead of hairlines.
Tradeoff: the spine is subtle at 2px — it must never carry alone what the header says.

4 — Tinted headers

Separate cards, each with a soft time-of-day wash on its header band. Most colorful and glanceable.
Tradeoff: tinted fills need their own dark-mode values, and it is the least Linear-quiet of the four.

1 — Split deck (from B)

Nav segment | input | Beacon in one 56px capsule. Everything is one thumb-reach surface.
Tradeoff: unlabeled icons, and the input gets ~180px of the width — tight once real text is in it.

2 — Stacked deck

The current dock distilled into one white capsule: full-width input on top, labeled tabs below. Most discoverable.
Tradeoff: tallest option (~96px), so it gives back some of the vertical space the redesign reclaims.

3 — Mode chip — PICKED, round 3

Now icon-only and detached: the active surface is its own little card beside the bar, with a small gap. Tapping it opens the switcher; /braindump, /chat still work as typed commands. The input gets its full width back and the two concerns read separately.
Tradeoff: an icon-only card must stay legible as 'you are here' — the lime tint carries that, so it needs a careful dark-mode value.

4 — Nav + capture split

A slim icons-only nav pill centered, capture as its own lime button (the omnibar opens as a sheet).
Tradeoff: capture costs a tap before typing, and the command palette feels hidden behind a '+' that promises 'add'.

Current (reference)

What ships today: header pill + week-nav pill stacked (two borders, two shadows), then the canvas panel, then the dock well holding notices, omnibar, and tab bar. Five bordered surfaces compete before any content appears — this is why it reads busy rather than professional.

B — Command Deck

Raycast-inspired: chrome nearly disappears. Title and a bare day strip sit straight on paper, content becomes one full-bleed sheet with hairline sections, and a single bottom capsule owns everything — tab icons, capture, and Beacon.
Its command bar and flat header carried into the synthesis.

C — Editorial Calm

Typography-led quiet: a Source Serif 'Today' headline on bare paper, a numeral day strip with a lime dot, bucket cards floating directly on the backdrop, and an icons-only tab row.
Its bucket cards carried into the synthesis; its serif header was explored and set aside.

Synthesis — serif header variant (not picked)

Kept for reference: same synthesis structure with C's Source Serif headline and numeral strip. Set aside in favor of the flat compact header.
